message.reasoning:
We need to call the function hypothesis_testing_ttest_ind with sample1, sample2, significance_level=0.05. Then we need to interpret the result. The function returns something; we need to see what it returns. We don't know the exact return format. But likely it returns an object with t-statistic, p-value, degrees of freedom, maybe confidence interval. We'll assume typical output: {t_statistic, p_value, df}. We'll then interpret: if p < alpha, reject null hypothesis that means equal means. Let's compute manually? Let's approximate: sample1 mean = (22+33+42+12+34)/5 = 143/5 = 28.6. sample2 mean = (23+45+44+14+38)/5 = 164/5 = 32.8. difference = -4.2. Standard deviations: sample1 variance: sum((x-mean)^2): (22-28.6)^2=43.56, (33-28.6)^2=19.36, (42-28.6)^2=176.36, (12-28.6)^2=273.16, (34-28.6)^2=29.16. Sum= 543.6? Let's sum: 43.56+19.36=62.92; +176.36=239.28; +273.16=512.44; +29.16=541.6. So variance = 541.6/(n-1)=541.6/4=135.4. SD = sqrt(135.4)=11.63. Sample2 variance: (23-32.8)^2=96.04, (45-32.8)^2=148.84, (44-32.8)^2=125.44, (14-32.8)^2=352.84, (38-32.8)^2=27.04. Sum: 96.04+148.84=244.88; +125.44=370.32; +352.84=723.16; +27.04=750.2. Variance=750.2/4=187.55. SD=sqrt(187.55)=13.69. Pooled standard error: sqrt(s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2) = sqrt(135.4/5 + 187.55/5) = sqrt(27.08 + 37.51) = sqrt(64.59)=8.04. t = (28.6-32.8)/8.04 = -4.2/8.04 = -0.522. Degrees of freedom: n1+n2-2=8. t critical for two-tailed alpha=0.05, df=8: t_crit ~ 2.306. Since |t|<t_crit, fail to reject null. p-value approx? For t=-0.522, df=8, p ~ 0.61. So we fail to reject. So conclusion: no significant difference.
